batchName: Roman Religion and Mythology (753 BC-AD 391) - Latin words
description: Written by hand from the chapter text: the Latin words it explains

questions.question: What does do ut des mean?
questions.explanation: Roman religion worked almost like a business contract with the gods.
questions.sourceQuote: summed up in the phrase *do ut des*: "I give, that you might give."

questions.question: Who were the Vestals, the virgines Vestales?
options: Six priestesses who tended Vesta’s sacred flame
Priests who read the flight of birds
questions.explanation: A Vestal who broke her vow of chastity was buried alive.
questions.sourceQuote: The Vestals (*virgines Vestales*) were Rome's most famous priesthood

questions.question: Who was the paterfamilias in a Roman home?
options: The father of the family, who acted as its priest
questions.explanation: He made daily offerings; his wife looked after the worship of Vesta at the hearth.
questions.sourceQuote: The father of the family (*paterfamilias*) acted as its priest

questions.question: What did the Romans mean by pietas?
options: Dutiful care in keeping good relations with the gods
questions.explanation: Romans credited their rise to world power to it.
questions.sourceQuote: their piety (*pietas*), the dutiful care with which they kept good relations with the gods.

questions.question: What was a templum to an augur?
options: A sacred space marked out by ritual
questions.explanation: Only later did the word come to mean a temple building.
questions.sourceQuote: called a *templum*, a word that only later came to mean a temple building.

questions.question: What was evocatio?
options: Inviting an enemy’s god to change sides
Calling up the spirits of the dead
questions.explanation: At Veii a Roman commander promised the city’s goddess Juno a new home in Rome.

questions.question: What was the mola salsa that the Vestals prepared?
options: Salted flour sprinkled on sacrificial animals
A honey cake for the Lares
questions.explanation: It was used in every official sacrifice.
questions.sourceQuote: They prepared the *mola salsa*, a salted flour sprinkled on each animal before it was killed

questions.question: What does Dis Manibus, written on Roman tombstones, mean?
questions.explanation: The dead were believed to join the spirits of the underworld.
questions.sourceQuote: tombstones were commonly dedicated "to the spirit-gods" (*Dis Manibus*).
